exposure: Somatosensory-evoked potentials (SEPs) (median nerve) performed in the first 14 days of life
Pathological SEPs (unilateral or bilateral absence of N20, or unilateral or bilateral latency >= 36 ms)
outcome: Moderate-to-severe alteration on basal ganglia-thalamic (BGT) and/or white matter areas on cerebral resonance imaging (MRI) at 7-14 days of life
Neurodevelopmental impairment (global Brunet-Lezine test score < 70) at two years of age
cohort: 84 neonates born at >= 36 weeks gestational age with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) treated with therapeutic hypothermia (TH).
finding: Somatosensory-evoked potentials (SEPs) performed in the first two weeks of life in newborns with HIE and TH demonstrated good predictive capacity for detecting increased risk of neuroimaging lesions and neurodevelopmental impairment at two years of age.
